summary.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA margin at 7.99%, up 121 bps.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income for Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) was INR115.44 crore, up 15.68% YoY, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore and net profit up 35% to INR6.40 crore. Management reiterated the INR500 crore FY27 revenue target and signalled FY28 revenue above INR600 crore, while holding debt flat and FCF near INR8-9 crore a year. Q1 CCTV and vocational training segments made losses, which management attributed to project timing. On the call, the company also declined a buyback proposal, citing growth plans and IPO funds still unspent.

financial_highlights.value: INR69 crore debt vs ~INR60 crore cash

segments.name: Security (manpower)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue INR54.98 crore; manpower businesses (security, housekeeping, payroll) EBITDA margin stated at around 9.95%.

segments.name: CCTV / electronic security
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue INR2.11 crore; loss of about INR1.27 lakh at PAT level, attributed to project-stage costs ahead of billing. Management calls it the most profitable segment and expects stabilisation by September quarter.

segments.name: Vocational training (LLP and Keertika Academy)
segments.commentary: Net loss of about INR57 lakh in Q1; reported vocational training revenue as nil (INR0 lakh).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of above INR500 crore; management expects to cross it at the current year-on-year pace, helped by contracts that started in late FY26 being billed for a full year.
FY27 revenue growth guided at about 12-15% earlier; management said hope to grow about 20% while protecting balance sheet.
EBITDA margin: no firm expansion number for FY27 since Q1 is seasonally strongest; CEO expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over next 2 years.
FY27 CCTV/project revenue expected around INR30 crore (vs INR13-14 crore in FY26), with PAT rising to INR3.5-4 crore (from about INR2.5 crore last year).
FY28 revenue expected to cross INR600 crore, with management targeting INR630-650 crore.
Debt levels expected to stay flat in FY27 and FY28; FCF aim to rise from INR8-9 crore average to INR13-14 crore if systems revenue grows from INR13-14 crore to about INR30 crore.
capex_capacity: DDU-GKY skill development project for Odisha (INR7.93 crore order, two-year contract); expected billing about INR4 crore this year, with about six months of infrastructure set-up before training starts.

HDFC Bank command-and-control centre (CCTV-driven, subscription model) under final negotiation; set-up investment about INR1-1.5 crore, expected revenue INR1.5-2 crore; scope could cover 100-150 branches.
Pipeline of Mumbai police and traffic CCTV tenders of INR15-18 crore; Mumbai traffic tender of INR2.18 crore already won.
AMC contract from New Kolkata Development Authority (about INR6 crore) in final tender stage; SAIL Burnpur engagement targeted INR4-5 crore this year.
Management is exploring AI-driven cleaning machines and mechanised facade cleaning (Kolkata Airport) to lift gross margins.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 order wins: 5 Reliance Projects and Property Management Services work orders worth INR30.77 crore; 7 Reliance Group FM contracts worth INR14.94 crore (combined INR45.71 crore); 2 Nesco Limited orders worth INR1.94 crore; West Bengal Public Department order of INR36.71 lakh.
Government manpower tenders are priced at L1 around 3.85% on GeM; management is becoming selective in manpower and focusing on CCTV and DDU-GKY projects and banking and manufacturing clients.
Client renewal rate stated at about 96-97%; average client retention of 4.5-5 years.

Top clients: Reliance about INR46-47 crore; HDFC Bank about INR18 crore; Anjali Jewellers about INR12 crore; airports about INR30 crore combined; Torrent Power about INR6-7 crore. DTET contract renewal pending, and management is provisioning for possible loss.
West Bengal accounts for about 72-73% of revenue; management expects this share to remain broadly stable, with Bihar and Odisha expansion underway.
Working capital cycle about 3 months (DSO ~3 months); CCTV carries the longest working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Given guidance of 12-15% growth and INR500 crore revenue, is there scope to raise FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kanad Mukherjee said FY27 should cross INR500 crore at the current pace, aided by full-year billing of FY26 wins; Q1 is seasonally the strongest margin quarter, so margin expansion is hard to predict.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 segment revenue mix and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Security INR54.98 crore, housekeeping INR41.88 crore, IFM INR10.28 crore, payroll INR3.40 crore, CCTV INR2.11 crore, small security and housekeeping INR1.29 crore; manpower EBITDA margin about 9.95%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and FCF outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt to remain flat in FY27 and FY28. FCF has averaged INR8-9 crore over three to four years; management aims for INR13-14 crore if systems revenue rises to about INR30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach about 20%, and what margin trajectory is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes to grow about 20% without compromising balance sheet, by being selective on contracts. The CEO expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin improvement over the next two years from electronics and mechanisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt, and why are short-term loans and advances high?
qa_highlights.answer: At June 2026, standalone cash about INR60 crore against debt INR69 crore; consolidated debt about INR82 crore. Advances are vendor advances for IFM projects, circular in nature, and include related-party loans to Keertika Academy.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company do a buyback given the share price fall from the IPO price?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO declined, saying IPO capital is for growth in electronics, skill development and working capital; he said returns to investors could come later. About INR36.85 crore of IPO funds remain unutilised.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CCTV loss-making in Q1 and what is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Project businesses incur costs before completion certificates and billing, which typically land in July-August; the same happened last year (loss about INR1.5 crore). FY28 revenue expected above INR600 crore, targeting INR630-650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top client exposures and contract durations?
qa_highlights.answer: Reliance is the top client (about INR46-47 crore, open-ended yearly renewal, served 14-15 years); HDFC about INR18 crore; Anjali Jewellers about INR12 crore. Nesco is yearly renewal, WBSEDCL a two-year contract, DDU-GKY Odisha two years.

risks_watch: CCTV/project segment remained loss-making in Q1; management expects stabilisation by September quarter billing. Watch whether losses reverse.
Concentration: Reliance about 8-9% of revenue, and West Bengal about 72-73% of revenue.
Pending DTET renewal, for which the company is provisioning for a possible loss.
Manpower business is increasingly GeM L1-priced at 3.85%, which could pressure margins on non-GeM contracts.
Management said Q2 and Q3 margins tend to moderate; FY27 margin expansion not assured.
Capital allocation: buyback declined, with about INR36.85 crore IPO funds unspent; stock price weak versus IPO price of INR111 (about INR46 at call time, per analyst).
Working capital at about 3 months and rising vendor advances may constrain FCF.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and FY28 targets, but cautious on margin expansion, which management said is hard to forecast given seasonality and the commoditised mix. Evasive on the buyback and on the share price decline, which it answered by stressing growth capital needs.
key_quotes: So what we are seeing is that, last year we would have -- whatever revenues we had booked from November-December onwards that will get booked for the entire year during this financial year.
There will be no increase in debt. Debt levels will stay the same.
So the hope is to grow at 20% definitely. But also while ensuring that the strength of the balance sheet is not compromised.

HDFC Bank command-and-control CCTV centre (set-up investment INR1-1.5 crore, under final negotiation, scope 100-150 branches)

growth.why: Management reiterates above INR500 crore FY27 revenue (about 20% growth hoped for, vs earlier 12-15%) and FY28 INR630-650 crore, backed by Q1 order wins of INR45.71 crore and a INR7.93 crore DDU-GKY order, though most named items are contracts or pipeline rather than specific capacity and timelines are partly unclear.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: CEO expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over 2 years from electronics and mechanisation, but no firm FY27 number as Q1 margin (7.99%, +121 bps) is seasonally strongest and Q2/Q3 tend to moderate.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New set-ups are small: DDU-GKY Odisha order INR7.93 crore needs ~6 months infrastructure before training, and HDFC CCTV centre needs INR1-1.5 crore set-up investment, still under final negotiation; no plant or line capacity is named.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 order wins of INR45.71 crore, FY27 revenue to cross INR500 crore (vs INR115.44 crore Q1 total income, ~15.7% YoY), and FY28 revenue guided at INR630-650 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure given and the business is asset-light manpower; growth is met with about INR36.85 crore of unspent IPO funds, and capex items are small (INR1-1.5 crore HDFC set-up).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management hopes for about 20% growth vs earlier 12-15% guidance and says FY27 should cross INR500 crore at current pace, but margin upgrade is not assured given seasonality.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include DTET renewal pending with a provision for possible loss, GeM L1 pricing at ~3.85% on manpower tenders, and CCTV losses in Q1 that management expects to reverse only by September quarter billing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is exploring AI-driven cleaning machines and mechanised facade cleaning (Kolkata Airport) to lift gross margins, but no launch date is given.

rows.label: Q1 FY27 order wins INR45.71 crore; CCTV revenue ~INR30 crore in FY27
rows.why: Q1 Reliance and Reliance Group orders of INR45.71 crore plus CCTV revenue guided to about INR30 crore in FY27 vs INR13-14 crore in FY26, with CCTV PAT rising to INR3.5-4 crore from about INR2.5 crore.

rows.label: Debt flat; FCF to rise to INR13-14 crore
rows.why: Debt is expected flat in FY27 and FY28 (consolidated INR82 crore), and FCF could go from INR8-9 crore average to INR13-14 crore only if systems revenue rises to about INR30 crore.

rows.label: Working capital and vendor advances
rows.why: DSO about 3 months, CCTV carries the longest working capital, and vendor advances for IFM projects are high, which may constrain FCF.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR500 crore FY27 and INR630-650 crore FY28 revenue targets and on the CCTV ramp, but cautious and evasive on margin expansion, the buyback and the share price fall below the IPO price. Analysts pushed on guidance upgrades, margins, net debt and high short-term advanc

quality.why: Consolidated total income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, but the brief does not state whether volume, price or mix drove it, and it cites no one-off gains or low-base effects; the CCTV and vocational losses are operating timing issues, not growth one-offs.
